evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 11.29 mg/L at 50.0 h to 2.05 at 50.2 h and remains 1.2-2.0 mg/L through 52 h (receiving_observations), violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO2 prior to 50 h tracked sources (~11-13 mg/L); P assay at 48 h = 3.11 g/L matches sources (3.0-3.1 g/L), so growth is normal and the fault is oxygen supply
physical_forward_model at h 52 estimates transfer multiplier ~0.407 of nominal, indicating aeration/transfer failure

Forward-model comparison: strong_feed_reduction yields lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (7.27 mg·h/L) and highest min DO (0.92 mg/L) while retaining ~194 kg product; increase_air alone (deficit 11.61) is insufficient at 40% transfer capacity
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~50.2 h to 1.2-2.0 mg/L (below the 2.0 mg/L minimum) while product formation tracked the source batches, indicating a sudden loss of oxygen-transfer capacity (model-estimated multiplier ~0.41 of nominal). A 15% aeration increase alone cannot close the deficit; the forward model consistently shows strong_feed_reduction (40% feed cut, 15% more air) gives the smallest residual oxygen deficit and highest minimum DO while retaining full product mass (~194 kg). Stop is rejected as it yields zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; even under strong feed reduction, sensitivity members show residual DO violations (min DO range ~0.5-1.4 mg/L), so full constraint satisfaction is not guaranteed. If the transfer failure partially self-recovers or is worse than estimated, the ranking of feed cuts vs aeration could shift, but strong feed reduction is the least-violating option across members and costs no product mass.
